newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 2.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--An obviously expedient "procedural dialogue" between Greece and Turkey has begun, giving Turkey the opportunity to lay on the table the claims it has long had against Greece. Greece, on the other hand, has the chance to alleviate the international pressure to appear more conciliatory in its relations with Ankara and to highlight Turkey's agressive stance. Meetings between the two governments are expected to be scheduled for May 20 in the Dutch capital.

--Labour's triumphant win in yesterday's British elections means support for Cyprus's accession to the European Union but lukewarm support for a return of the Elgin Marbles: Shadow foreign secretary Robin Cook said a resolution of the Cyprus problem should not hold up the island republic's entry to the bloc, but that the Parthenon friezes were "safe" in Britain.

--Ankara is bringing along its best-known 'hawks' to the dialogue it is beginning with Greece. In two meetings in 24 hours, Foreign Ministers Theodoros Pangalos and Tansu Ciller insisted on the need for a speedy resolution of problems.

--A group of concerned citizens yesterday began their campaign, on the 21st anniversary of the death of Alekos Panagoulis, to give the first man to effectively resist the 1967 colonel's dictatorship the place he deserves.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis is reportedly dissatisfied with leaks to the press regarding a forthcoming reshuffle and internal party dissent. He is expected to pull renegade ruling party PASOK members into line when he addresses the party's Parliamentary Group next Wednesday.
--Road fatalities are falling across Europe but for Greece, due to the absence of the state. Proposals to improve Greece's record were submitted a year ago and have yet to be implemented.
--An organised campaign by residents in Athens has seen more than 200 new parking meters sabotaged by silicone.
--Yesterday's spring rains failed to deter some 6,000 from turning out to the three rallies to celebrate Labour Day in Greece. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
